answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must register identities by burning cryptographic stake scaled superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot n^2$, imposing exponential economic friction against mass duplication. Each verified node commits a permanent relic of burned collateral, anchoring its identity in the ledger like indelible pigment on parchment. When competing for work, an agent proving identity verification commits stake harder than crafting a sonnet, guaranteeing attacker cost outpaces linear revenue.
